extracted.intended_audience: typesetters, printers, editors, and copyeditors (academic/press production staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and production standards for typography, punctuation, abbreviations, capitalization, accents, and related house-style conventions used by a university press (Manual of Style / specimens of type). Useful for copyeditors and compositors producing print material to press standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'A' and 'an' usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A' and 'an': use of, before h and u; spacing of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entry: "'A' and 'an': use of, before h and u, 114; spacing of, 268." (See referenced sections for detailed rules on when to use 'a' vs 'an' before h- and u- words and spacing conventions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: "a-" (negative particle) compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: "a-" (negative particle), compounds with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entry pointing to section 205 for rules on forming compounds with the negative particle 'a-'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations (forms and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations: in literary references, no.; no space between elements of, 52, 103; not to be divided, 219; of academic titles, 22; of biblical and apocryphal books, list of, 109; of names of states, 106; of technical terms, list of, in; of titles of publications, omission of period after initials used for, 123; rules for, 106-11; use of apostrophe in, 123; of period after, 123.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive entry pointing to multiple sections: rules for abbreviation form, spacing (no space between elements), where to omit periods (e.g., initials for publication titles), nondivision of abbreviations at line breaks, lists of standard abbreviations for academic titles, biblical books, states and technical terms, and punctuation rules (periods, apostrophes). See referenced sections for authoritative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of -able and -ible
rubrics_metrics.description: "-able" and "-ible," in divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index pointer (224) for hyphenation/division rules when breaking words ending in -able/-ible across lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic degrees: abbreviation & capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic degrees, abbreviation and capitalization of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index references (21-22) for how to abbreviate and capitalize academic degrees (e.g., B.A., Ph.D.) according to house style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accents: retention in foreign words
rubrics_metrics.description: Accents, retention of, in foreign words incorporated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index pointer (59) indicating the press's rule on whether to retain diacritical marks in foreign loanwords incorporated into English — see section 59 for particulars and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of words with acquired/limited/special meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquired, limited, or special meaning, words having, capitalization of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index pointer (25) for when to capitalize words that have acquired specific or restricted senses; see examples and rules in the referenced section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of juridical Acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts, juridical, capitalization of names of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index pointer (18) giving rule for capitalization of names of legal/juridical acts (statutes, acts), e.g., when to capitalize 'Act', proper names, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.D. (anno Domini) formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: A.D. (anno Domini): spacing of; use of small caps for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index notes: spacing rules (52, 219) and recommendation to use small caps for 'A.D.' (see section 52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of titles in direct address
rubrics_metrics.description: Address, capitalization of titles in direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index pointer (21) for rules on capitalizing titles when used in direct address (e.g., 'Dear Sir').

rubrics_metrics.name: Address line setting (letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address line: at end of letters, etc., how to set; at opening of letters, etc., how to set; omission of comma after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index references (50, 64, 161) for layout and punctuation of address lines both at letter openings and closings, including when to omit the comma after the address line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotype accents — modern (point-size tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: MONOTYPE ACCENTS— MODERN: point-size specific accent tables (e.g., 11-point No. 8—lower case italic; 11-point No. 8—italic caps; 11-point No. 8—roman lower case; 11-point No. 8—roman caps; 11-point No. 8—roman small caps, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pages contain detailed specimen tables showing which accented characters and caps/small caps/italic forms are available for specific monotype sizes (11, 9, 8, 7, 6 point, etc.). Use these tables to select correct accent glyphs for the given point size and style; see the listed point-size subsections for exact glyph availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotype accents — old style (point-size tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: MONOTYPE ACCENTS— OLD STYLE: listings of accent availability across six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve point sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with modern monotype accents, these tables indicate which accented glyphs and caps/small caps are available in old-style monotype faces at each point size. Refer to the specific point-size table when setting type to ensure appropriate accents are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotype combination braces and miscellaneous monotype
rubrics_metrics.description: MONOTYPE COMBINATION BRACES — 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, AND 12 POINT; MISCELLANEOUS MONOTYPE (numbered specimens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies available monotype combination braces and other miscellaneous monotype figures (e.g., six-point number plates). Use these designated combination sizes when composing material requiring braces or special monotype elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface specimens: include samples across fonts and sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIMENS OF TYPES IN USE — multiple named faces (CHELTENHAM, CHELTENHAM CONDENSED, CHELTENHAM BOLD EXTRA CONDENSED, CHELTENHAM BOLD CONDENSED, CLARENDON, BELLA ROBBIA, DELLA ROBBIA, etc.) shown at many point sizes (6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 18, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72, 96, 120, 144, 180, 216 point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual provides printed specimens of many named typefaces at a broad range of point sizes. Use these specimens as a reference for how each face renders at specific sizes and for selecting appropriate faces for headings, text, initials, and display purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accented letters — six to twelve point
rubrics_metrics.description: ACCENTED LETTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT (lists of accented glyphs for multiple faces in that size range).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For small-size settings (6–12 point), specimens show accented capitals and lowercase glyphs for each face; use these when setting foreign words or names at small sizes to ensure correct accent forms are available and legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters — all sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIAL CHARACTERS — ALL SIZES (display of ampersand, currency, punctuation, ligatures, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens display special characters for many faces and sizes; consult them to confirm glyph shapes and availabilities (e.g., ampersand, currency symbols, ligatures) before composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initials (drop caps) — multiple sizes and faces
rubrics_metrics.description: INITIALS — presented at large display sizes (thirty-six, forty-eight, seventy-two point, etc.) in faces such as BURFORD, DELLA ROBBIA, ROYCROFT, JENSON, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual specifies a catalog of initial initials in different faces and sizes for use as display initials/drop caps. Choose initials and sizes appropriate to page layout and match face/style to body text when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornaments (printer's ornaments) — numbered catalogue
rubrics_metrics.description: ORNAMENTS — numbered plates (e.g., plates 28, 39, 52, 54–57, 67, etc.) showing various ornaments across many pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual catalogs ornament figures by plate number. Use the indicated ornament numbers when specifying decorative elements in layout or when ordering/calling up ornament plates for composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borders — specified point widths and numbered designs
rubrics_metrics.description: BORDERS — TWO POINT NO. ONE; THREE POINT NO. TWO; FOUR POINT NO. FOUR; etc.; also larger sizes (twelve point, twenty-four point, thirty, thirty-six, forty-eight point numbered border designs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a catalog of border designs by point thickness and plate number for use in layout framing. Specify both point size and plate number to reproduce the exact border design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brass rule faces and line rules
rubrics_metrics.description: BRASS RULE FACES — hairline (on one- and two-point body), dotted (on one-point body), dotted (on two-point body), hairline parallel (on two-point body), half-point side face (on two-point body), one-point side face (on two- and three-point body); available in two point, three point, four point, eight point, ten point, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the available brass rule faces and thicknesses for rule lines and borders. Use the correct rule face and body thickness when specifying thin/dotted/hairline rules in printed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescription signs and advertising figures
rubrics_metrics.description: PRESCRIPTION SIGNS; ADVERTISING FIGURES — numbered specimen figures (e.g., advertising figures in eighteen point, thirty point, outline styles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog entries for prescription and advertising-specific symbols/figures; consult specimens to select the appropriate figure size and style for medical/advertising composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typewriter and reproducing typewriter specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: REPRODUCING TYPEWRITER and NEW MODEL ELITE/REMINGTON TYPEWRITER specimens shown at six, ten, twelve point settings with multi-line examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens indicate appearance of typewriter faces at standard sizes; use these to match monospaced/typewriter text or to select a typewriter face for setting correspondence, tables, or reproduced typed matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual of Style: index and cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: INDEX TO MANUAL — entries provide cross-reference pointers to detailed rules (e.g., the index lists many topical entries and the section numbers to consult).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index is a navigational rubric: when editing or composing, consult the listed section numbers for authoritative rules and examples on specific topics (punctuation, capitalization, abbreviations, hyphenation, accents, addresses, etc.).
